best_for: Windows users who copy and paste all day, such as writers, coders and support staff, and keep losing the thing they copied five minutes ago.

points.title: Every copy is kept
points.text: Ditto saves each item you copy to a local database. Press Ctrl and the backtick key, or click the tray icon, then pick an older clip and press Enter to paste it into the window you were in.

points.title: Not just text
points.text: It stores text, images, HTML and custom clipboard formats. Shift-Enter pastes as plain text, which strips formatting when you move text between apps.

points.title: Groups for clips you reuse
points.text: Put snippets you paste often, like addresses or boilerplate replies, into groups, and nest groups inside each other. Keyboard shortcuts move clips between groups without touching the Windows clipboard.

points.title: Stays on your PC
points.text: The project describes Ditto as local first: no login, no cloud and no telemetry. It is free and open source under GPL-3.0, with a PayPal link if you want to give something back.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version. Since version 3.25.113.0 the installer covers 64-bit and Arm64 PCs, and a portable zip runs without installing.

points.title: What is listed here
points.text: The installer here is x64 and installs for all users, so it needs administrator rights. The Windows listing keeps 7 versions.
